outcome_detail: $25 million settlement paid by the City of San Mateo to three women, finalized in March 2024 — reported as the city's largest-ever lawsuit settlement.
criminal_detail: Noah Winchester was charged in July 2016 and convicted in October 2019 of raping and sexually assaulting five women while on duty — three between July 2013 and October 2015 while a San Mateo police officer and two while a Los Rios Community College District officer — on counts including kidnapping with intent to commit rape, rape, and sexual penetration and oral copulation under color of authority. He was sentenced in February 2020 to 81 years to life in prison.
incident_date_approx: On-duty assaults between 2013 and 2015; the San Mateo assaults occurred between July 2013 and October 2015.
description: Three women who were sexually assaulted on duty by former San Mateo police officer Noah Winchester sued the City of San Mateo in 2022, alleging the police department was grossly negligent in hiring him and ignored red flags, including prior police reports identifying him as a sexual-assault suspect during his earlier employment as a Los Rios Community College District officer. Winchester was convicted in 2019 of raping and assaulting five women while on duty and was sentenced to 81 years to life in prison. The women were able to sue under California Assembly Bill 1455, which extended the statute of limitations for victims of sexual abuse by law enforcement officers from two to ten years. In March 2024 the city finalized a $25 million settlement with the three women, its largest lawsuit settlement ever.
